review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped for uses of the sectorCurve_* lemmas in SectorCurveLemma.lean. The file has no @[simp] declarations at all. The sectorCurve definition is an if-then-else chain, so simp cannot evaluate it at the knots without unfolding. I did not recommend simp attributes for the segment lemmas (seg1/2/3, norm_seg*). They carry membership hypotheses and range over intervals, so simp is a poor fit for them. I did not run Lean, so the claim that the knot lemmas would fire under plain simp is untested. A possible conflict is that simp might rewrite `sectorCurve r α 1` to `↑r` where a downstream proof expects the unfolded form. I did not check the rest of the repo for such cases.

findings.excerpt:
theorem sectorCurve_zero (r : ℝ) (α : ℝ) :
    sectorCurve r α 0 = 0 := by simp [sectorCurve]
findings.problem: The closed-form values of the piecewise-defined `sectorCurve` at the knots 0, 1 and 3 are stated as plain theorems with no `@[simp]` attribute. The definition is an `if` chain, so plain `simp` cannot evaluate `sectorCurve r α 0`, `sectorCurve r α 1` or `sectorCurve r α 3` without unfolding. Downstream proofs therefore have to name the lemmas by hand in `simp only [...]` or `rw [...]`, as the sites in SectorCurveLemma.lean show. Each statement is a literal-argument evaluation with a canonical right-hand side (`0` or `↑r`), so there is no looping or ambiguity risk. The neighbouring `sectorCurve_two` has a non-normal RHS and should stay non-simp.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `sectorCurve_zero`, `sectorCurve_three` and `sectorCurve_one`. Then downstream uses can drop the explicit lemma names, for example `simp only [F, sectorCurve_zero, sectorCurve_three, ...]` in SectorCurveLemma.lean line 141 and the `rw [..., sectorCurve_zero, sectorCurve_three, sub_self]` at line 264. `sectorCurve_closed` and `sectorCurve_passes_through_origin` would then follow by `simp`. Leave the `if`-unfolding definition itself non-simp. Keep `sectorCurve_two`, the segment lemmas and the norm lemmas as ordinary lemmas, because they have side conditions or non-canonical right-hand sides.
findings.benefit: Endpoint evaluations such as `F 3 - F 0` become automatic under `simp`. Users no longer need `simp [sectorCurve]`, which exposes the `if` chain and can pull in unwanted case splits.
